name: table
purpose: Composition primitives for building accessible, pixel-perfect data tables, in two modes. **Composition mode** (default): compose the anatomy by hand (header / body / rows / cells) — the component owns markup, tokens, a11y, configurable column sizing (an emphasized first column), sortable headers, selectable rows, and a **freeze system** for sticky columns (e.g. an actions column) and a sticky header. **Data-driven mode**: pass `data` + `columns` and the table renders itself via the headless **`@tanstack/vue-table`** engine, still rendering through the same primitives (our markup/tokens/a11y, pixel-perfect to Figma). Pairs with the [`Pagination`](pagination.md) component (rendered automatically in the footer when `paginated`). A top **toolbar band** (`title` / `toolbar` / `filters` slots) sits above the scroll viewport in both modes for a title, search / filter / export / column-selector actions, and removable filter chips; the `toolbar` and `filters` slots are scoped with the TanStack `table` instance (in data-driven mode) so the consumer can drive filtering, global search, and column visibility through the table's own methods. **Engine.** Data-driven mode is driven by **`@tanstack/vue-table`** (`useVueTable` + `getCoreRowModel` / `getSortedRowModel` / `getFilteredRowModel` / `getPaginationRowModel`), covering sorting, pagination, row selection, column visibility, and global filtering — client- and server-side (`manualSorting` / `manualPagination` / `manualFiltering`). It is a pure-logic library (no markup/styles/positioning/animation), granted narrowly to this single component per [`.claude/rules/dependencies.md`](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.claude/rules/dependencies.md) § Exceptions; rendering stays 100% in our primitives. State is exposed via v-model (`sorting`, `rowSelection`, `columnVisibility`, `globalFilter`, `pagination`, plus the structured `filters` model and the aggregate `state` snapshot below). `@tanstack/virtual` remains forbidden: the opt-in `virtual` mode windows the rows itself (spacer padding above and below the rendered slice, sized from a height index: each rendered row is measured with a `ResizeObserver`, rows not yet rendered take the average of the first rows measured, and when a row above the rows in view changes height the scroll position moves by the same amount so the rows in view stay still). Without `virtual`, a list of more than 200 rows renders its first 50 rows and mounts the rest as a spacer below them nears the viewport (an `IntersectionObserver`), so a long page costs what is on screen. **Toolbar & imperative API.** The toolbar band composes context-aware controls that drive the table through the injected context with no wiring: `Table.Filter` (a structured field/operator/value builder that commits removable/editable filter chips, with an escape slot to plug a custom builder such as the console's AQL), `Table.AppliedFilters` (the chips), `Table.ColumnSelector` (a column-visibility picker over the existing `columnVisibility` state), `Table.Export` (CSV download), and `Table.RefreshButton`. Structured filters are a first-class model (`v-model:filters`, an `AppliedFilter[]` distinct from the free-text `globalFilter`) mapped to the TanStack column filters client-side, or emitted for a server refetch under `manualFiltering`. A `loading` prop renders skeleton rows for dynamic (server-side) data. The root exposes a **curated imperative API** via `defineExpose` (`reload`, `clearFilters`, `exportCsv`, `getState`, `setState`) so controls or logic outside the table can drive it through a template ref, and a serializable `TableStateSnapshot` (`sorting` / `pagination` / `columnVisibility` / `columnOrder` / `globalFilter` / `filters`) is exposed via `v-model:state` + `getState()` / `setState()` + an `initialState` seed — the component stays router-agnostic, so the consuming app owns any URL / localStorage persistence. CSV serialization lives in a pure util at [`@aziontech/webkit/utils/csv`](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/packages/webkit/src/utils/csv.ts) (`toCsv` + `downloadCsv`). **Types** (declared in `injection-key.ts`, re-exported for consumers): `FilterOperator` = `'eq' | 'neq' | 'contains' | 'not-contains' | 'starts-with' | 'ends-with' | 'gt' | 'gte' | 'lt' | 'lte' | 'in' | 'not-in' | 'is-empty' | 'is-not-empty'`; `FilterField` = `{ id: string; label: string; type: 'text' | 'number' | 'select' | 'multi-select' | 'boolean' | 'date'; operators?: FilterOperator[]; options?: { label: string; value: string | number | boolean }[] }`; `AppliedFilter` = `{ field: string; operator: FilterOperator; value: string | number | boolean | Array<string | number>; label?: string }`; `TableStateSnapshot` = `{ sorting?: SortingState; pagination?: PaginationState; columnVisibility?: VisibilityState; columnOrder?: string[]; globalFilter?: string; filters?: AppliedFilter[] }` (every field optional so `setState` / `initialState` accept a partial; JSON-serializable). **Collections.** `useCollection` (`@aziontech/webkit/use-collection`) drives the data-driven mode in both client and server modes: `tableProps` binds `data` (one page), `columns` (ordered by the saved preferences), `rowKey`, `loading`, `sorting`, `manualSorting` / `manualFiltering` / `manualPagination`, `paginated`, `pagination`, `rowCount`, `rowsPerPageOptions`, `enableRowSelection`, `rowSelection`, `columnVisibility` and the three display preferences (`density`, `wrapLines`, `striped`) together with their update handlers, and `exportRows`, in one `v-bind`. The table keeps rendering one page; the composable owns filtering, sorting, paging and selection across pages, so `exportRows` hands `Table.Export` and `exportCsv()` every match rather than the page: in client mode the matching items (or every item for the `all` scope), in server mode what the collection's `exportAll` callback loads (the loaded page when there is none). **Cell presets and reordering.** Six presets render the cells every list repeats, each inside a `#cell-<id>` slot: `Table.CellLink` (a name that leaves the screen: an optional muted leading glyph (`icon`) for the provider or resource type, a 12 px external mark, a tooltip naming the destination, underline on hover, no mark without a destination; optional `+N` overflow through `OverflowCount` and a copy button pinned to the end edge), `Table.CellId` (an identifier with its copy button), `Table.CellStatus` (one semantic `Tag`), `Table.CellTags` (as many tags as fit, the rest behind `+N`), `Table.CellTime` (avatar of the author plus a relative time that updates every minute, the absolute time on the tooltip and for screen readers) and `Table.CellActions` (the row menu named after the row). `reorderable` adds a leading grip column: drag a grip with the pointer, or focus it and press Arrow Up, Arrow Down, Home or End; the table emits `update:data` with the reordered records and `reorder` with `{ from, to, row }`, announces every move in a polite status region and locks while a sort is applied; `rowReorderable` keeps chosen rows (a pinned default) in place.
useWhen: Records with the same fields shown in rows and columns, where the reader compares, sorts, selects or acts on rows (resource lists, logs, usage breakdowns).
A list needs a toolbar for search, structured filters, column visibility, CSV export or refresh — the `Table.*` toolbar parts drive the table through context.
Server-backed data that pages, sorts or filters on the API: `manual-pagination`, `manual-sorting` and `manual-filtering` emit the state instead of slicing locally.
avoidWhen: A short titled preview of a longer listing on a marketing page → use `listing-table`.
A feature-by-feature comparison of Azion with a competitor → use `comparison-table`.
Rows of mixed content (media, title, description, actions) that do not share columns → use `item`.
A grid of selectable cards or options → use `radio-cards`.
related: pagination` — the page strip; a data-driven table with `paginated` renders and wires it in the footer.
listing-table` — marketing section that composes `table` for a linked preview of a list.
empty-state` — the pattern behind the table's default `empty` slot; override the slot for resource-specific copy and actions.
item` — list rows without a column structure.
bestPractices: For repeated data, use data-driven mode: pass `data` + `columns` (any non-empty `columns` switches it on) and customize cells with the `cell-<columnId>` / `header-<columnId>` slots instead of composing N rows by hand. Compose `Table.Header` / `Table.Body` / `Table.Row` / `Table.Cell` only for small, static tables.
Give rows a stable id under `row-key` (default `'id'`); selection and `v-model:row-selection` are keyed by it.
Mark the row-actions column `kind: 'action'` so it pins to the trailing edge; give chip or short-token columns a `minWidth` rather than a fixed `width`.
Drive loading through the `loading` prop (skeleton rows, `aria-busy`) and keep the `empty` slot for no-data copy — do not swap the table for a spinner.

On a phone a console list keeps its grid and scrolls sideways (the default). Set `stackable` only for a short list read one record at a time on a narrow, phone-first surface (a marketing listing, a summary in a side panel), where a card per row reads better than a scroll; never on a resource index, a log or a list compared across columns.

Place `Table.Search`, `Table.Filter`, `Table.ColumnSelector`, `Table.Export` and `Table.RefreshButton` in the `toolbar` slot with no `v-model` wiring — they read the table from context. `Table.Search` and `Table.ColumnSelector` act on the TanStack instance, so they need data-driven mode.

props.name: maxHeight
props.doc: Max height (CSS length). The viewport scrolls dynamically: horizontal scroll appears automatically when columns overflow the width; vertical scroll appears only when `maxHeight` is set smaller than the content (under the sticky header).

props.name: bordered
props.doc: Draw the outer card border around the table. Off by default (the table is typically framed by a surrounding surface); set `bordered` / `:bordered="…"` to draw the `var(--border-default)` outline. The internal row dividers are unaffected.

props.name: data
props.doc: Data-driven mode: row records.

props.name: columns
props.doc: Data-driven mode: column definitions (`{ id?, accessorKey?, header?, label?, enableSorting?, grow?, principal?, frozen?, width?, minWidth?, align?, kind?, resizable?, hideable?, orderable? }`; `width` (px) sets a fixed pixel column (also needed when a frozen column precedes another frozen column on the same edge, so sticky offsets can be summed); **`minWidth`** (px) sets a **floor** instead: the table measures the column's own content — its header, including the sort affordance, and every rendered body cell — and pins the column to the larger of the two, as **one** width applied to the header and every body cell (a per-cell `min-width` would let each row size to its own content and drift the header away from the body). It is for a column whose content is a chip or a short token: a fixed `width` there is a bet in both directions — too generous and it reserves space the rest of the row needs, too tight and the chip inside it truncates. The measured width tracks the **rendered page**, so a column can change width when paging or sorting brings longer content into view; `width` wins when both are set, and a user resize wins over both. a `grow` column without `width` keeps a shared fixed basis so the header and body stay aligned and the cell never wraps. A column with no `grow` defaults to weight `2` for the **principal** column and `1` for the rest, so the columns fill the available space proportionally. The principal column is the one flagged `principal: true`, or — when none is flagged — the first non-action column. A `kind: 'action'` column is automatically pinned to the trailing (right) edge — staying reachable while the rest scrolls horizontally — and is never resizable. **`resizable: true`** opts a column into a live mouse/touch drag-to-resize handle on its header (native pointer events; the `@tanstack/vue-table` exception covers sorting/pagination/selection/visibility, not sizing). On the first drag of any divider every flexible column freezes at its current rendered width; from then on dragging changes **only that column** and the table grows (horizontal scroll) — the others are untouched. The drag floor is the column's own content width (header label + visible body cells), so a column never shrinks past its content. Frozen and action columns ignore `resizable`. **`label`** overrides the `Table.ColumnSelector` label when `header` is not a string; **`hideable: false`** excludes the column from `Table.ColumnSelector` (e.g. the actions column); **`orderable: true`** opts the column into `columnOrder`. When non-empty, the table renders itself via TanStack.

props.name: rowKey
props.doc: Field used as the stable row id (for selection).

props.name: enableSorting
props.doc: Enable sorting globally; per-column `enableSorting` overrides.

props.name: enableRowSelection
props.doc: Add a leading selection-checkbox column.

props.name: rowSelectable
props.doc: Data-driven mode: decides per row whether it can be selected (`(row) => row.kind === 'file'`). A row it rejects draws no checkbox, ignores row clicks and stays out of Select all.

props.name: selectOnRowClick
props.doc: Data-driven mode: clicking a row toggles its selection (requires `enableRowSelection`); interactive cells still own their own click.

props.name: headerKind
props.doc: Header density (data-driven): `compact` shrinks the column-header row's height and padding. Forwarded to the `TableHeader`'s `kind`.

props.name: paginated
props.doc: Render a Pagination in the footer.

props.name: pageSize
props.doc: Rows per page when paginated.

props.name: sorting
props.doc: v-model:sorting (TanStack SortingState).

props.name: rowSelection
props.doc: v-model:rowSelection (TanStack RowSelectionState).

props.name: columnVisibility
props.doc: v-model:columnVisibility (TanStack VisibilityState).

props.name: globalFilter
props.doc: v-model:globalFilter text.

props.name: pagination
props.doc: v-model:pagination (TanStack PaginationState).

props.name: manualSorting
props.doc: Server-side sorting: emit events, do not sort locally.

props.name: manualPagination
props.doc: Server-side pagination: emit events, do not slice locally.

props.name: manualFiltering
props.doc: Server-side filtering: emit events, do not filter locally.

props.name: rowCount
props.doc: Total row count for manual pagination.

props.name: rowsPerPageOptions
props.doc: Rows-per-page options shown in the footer selector.

props.name: loading
props.doc: Data-driven mode: render skeleton rows in the body (aligned to the visible columns) and set `aria-busy`; `Table.RefreshButton` disables/spins while true. Precedence: `loading` → skeleton, else rows, else `empty`.

props.name: filters
props.doc: v-model:filters — structured applied conditions committed by `Table.Filter`, distinct from `globalFilter`. Client-side they map to TanStack column filters; under `manualFiltering` they are emitted for a server refetch.

props.name: filterFields
props.doc: Field catalog the built-in `Table.Filter` builder offers (id, label, value type, allowed operators, select options). Omit and use `Table.Filter`'s default slot to plug a custom builder.

props.name: state
props.doc: v-model:state — an aggregate serializable snapshot layered over the per-concern models. A bound per-concern v-model (e.g. `v-model:sorting`) wins over `state` for that concern.

props.name: initialState
props.doc: Uncontrolled seed applied once on mount; seeds only concerns that are not bound to their own v-model.

props.name: exportRows
props.doc: Rows `Table.Export` and `exportCsv()` write for the `filtered` and `all` scopes in place of the rows the table holds (the `page` scope always writes the rendered page). `useCollection` binds it so an export covers every match, not only the page; a promise is awaited before the `export` event and the download.

props.name: exportFilename
props.doc: Default filename for `Table.Export` and `exportCsv()` when no per-call filename is given.

props.name: stackable
props.doc: Data-driven mode: opt in to stacked rows. When the table's own box is narrower than `--container-lg`, each row renders as a card of label and value pairs instead of the horizontally scrolling grid. Off by default: a console list scrolls sideways on a phone.

props.name: wrapLines
props.doc: Data-driven mode: cell text wraps onto several lines instead of truncating.

props.name: striped
props.doc: Data-driven mode: every other body row takes the raised surface.

props.name: density
props.doc: Row density: `compact` shrinks body rows and cell padding.

props.name: virtual
props.doc: Data-driven mode: render only the rows in view, for thousands of rows. The viewport scrolls vertically within `maxHeight` (40rem when empty). Ignored in the stacked layout.

props.name: estimateRowHeight
props.doc: Row height (px) assumed in `virtual` mode until a row is measured.

props.name: reorderable
props.doc: Data-driven mode: a leading grip column lets people drag rows, or move the focused grip's row with Arrow Up, Arrow Down, Home and End, into a new order. Emits `update:data` (bind `v-model:data`) and `reorder`; locked while a sort is applied.

props.name: rowReorderable
props.doc: With `reorderable`: decides per row whether it can move (`(row) => !row.locked`). A rejected row keeps its place: its grip is disabled, and no row is dropped onto it or moved past it with the keys.

props.name: getSubRows
props.doc: Data-driven mode: tree rows. Returns a row's children (`(row) => row.children`); a row with children gets an expand toggle in the principal column, its children render under it indented one step (`--spacing-md`) per level, and the grid element takes `role="treegrid"`. Sorting and filtering keep each child under its parent; selection is per row (selecting a parent does not select its children). `reorderable` is ignored in tree mode.

props.name: expanded
props.doc: v-model:expanded (TanStack ExpandedState: `true` for every row, or `{ [rowId]: true }`). Uncontrolled it starts collapsed.

events.name: row-click
events.notes: Fires when a rendered row is clicked (data-driven mode). `event` is the click; `row` is the clicked record.

events.name: update:state
events.notes: v-model:state; debounced so bursts of changes coalesce.

events.name: filter-apply
events.notes: The filter builder was committed (Apply) — the explicit re-query signal for `manualFiltering`.

events.name: refresh
events.notes: Refresh requested (`Table.RefreshButton` or `reload()`); the app refetches.

events.name: export
events.notes: Export requested with the resolved rows; a consumer may handle it server-side (otherwise the built-in CSV util downloads).

events.name: update:data
events.notes: reorderable`: the records in their new order; bind `v-model:data`.

events.name: reorder
events.payload: payload: { from: number; to: number; row: Record<string, unknown> }
events.notes: reorderable`: a row moved from index `from` to index `to` of `data`.

events.name: update:expanded
events.notes: Tree rows: v-model:expanded, after a toggle by pointer or keyboard.

slots.name: default
slots.notes: Composition mode: the scrollable region (TableCaption, TableHeader, TableBody).

slots.name: footer
slots.notes: Footer region rendered below the scroll viewport (e.g. TableFooter + Pagination), so it never scrolls with the body. In data-driven mode it renders automatically when `paginated`.

slots.name: caption
slots.notes: Data-driven mode: caption content (wrapped in TableCaption), fixed above the scroll viewport.

slots.name: title
slots.notes: Title text shown at the start of the toolbar band, fixed above the scroll viewport (both modes).

slots.name: toolbar
slots.notes: Action band (search, filter trigger, refresh, export, column-selector) above the scroll viewport, end-aligned beside the title. `table` is the TanStack instance in data-driven mode, `undefined` in composition mode; `selectedRows` / `selectedCount` / `clearSelection` expose the selection for bulk-action toolbars, and `loading` mirrors the prop.

slots.name: filters
slots.notes: Active-filter chips row below the toolbar (both modes); same scope as `toolbar`.

slots.name: empty
slots.notes: Data-driven mode: shown when there are no rows. Defaults to an empty-state block (illustration + title + description) following Figma; override the slot for custom copy/actions.
